name: Namibia
dated: Income Tax Act 1981 as in force from 2024-09-16 (Act 4 of 2024), NamibLII archived 2026-02-12
sources: Source: Income Tax Act 1981, NamibLII consolidation at 2024-09-16, archived copy `web.archive.org/web/20260212092155id_/https://namiblii.org/akn/na/act/1981/24/eng@2024-09-16` (`R4/na/law/namiblii_ita_2024-09-16_wayback20260212.txt`, html sha256 f8590e2fd0fb1b94…). vat.name: Value-Added Tax
vat.statute: Value-Added Tax Act 2000 s. 6 (1) (15 %), NamibLII point-in-time 2023-01-01 (Act 14 of 2022)
vat.doc: s. 6 (1) (as substituted by Act 6 of 2002): tax is charged "... at the rate of 15 per cent on the value of the supply or import". Text: NamibLII expression eng@2023-01-01 (the latest, after the Value-Added Tax Amendment Act 2022), archived copy web.archive.org/web/20241110061612id_/https://namiblii.org/akn/na/act/2000/10/eng@2023-01-01 (sha256 94a50d919b5ad094…), saved as na/law/namiblii_vat_2023-01-01_wayback20241110.txt.
notes: VAT 15 %; zero-rated basic foodstuffs and exempt supplies (Schedules IV, V) not separated from the basket lines

excise.name: Excise duties (SACU common excise tariff, Schedule 1 Part 2)
excise.statute: Customs and Excise Act 1998 (Act 20 of 1998) s. 1 ('"excise duty" ... means any duty leviable under Part 2 of Schedule 1 on any goods manufactured in Namibia'; excisable goods: goods specified in Part 2 of Schedule 1) and s. 54 (1) (the Minister amends any Schedule by notice 'in order to conform to any amendment made by any other country in the common customs area and in accordance with the obligations imposed by or under the Customs Union Agreement') [text version: lexifina/namibia-law, customs-excise, version in force from 2022-05-04 (source NamibLII akn/na/act/1998/20); its 'Schedules 1-8' unit prints no rates and lists the amending notices to GN 317 of 2022]; SACU Agreement 2002 (as amended 12 April 2013) art. 21 (1): the Ministers responsible for Finance of all Member States 'meet and agree on the rates of specific excise and ad valorem excise duties ... to be applied to goods grown, produced or manufactured in or imported into the Common Customs Area'; art. 22: similar legislation [text version: sacu.int SACU-Agreement.pdf, Wayback 20210517172146, R4/fetch/gap/sacu_agreement_wb20210517.pdf]; rates: the SACU common rates as in SA Act 45 of 2024 Part I (to 11 March 2025) and Act 3 of 2026 Sch. II (from 12 March 2025); the Namibia dollar is at par with the rand
excise.doc: 2024/2025 rates: SA Act 45 of 2024 s. 1 (2) ('deemed to have come into operation on 21 February 2024') and Part I: '104.10.20 2203.00.90 Other R135.89/li aa', '104.15.03 2204.21.41 ... R5.57/li', '104.23.05 2208.30.10 ... R274.39/li aa', '104.30.07 2402.20.90 Other R10.89/10 cigarettes'; 2025/2026 rates: SA Act 3 of 2026 s. 4 (2) (12 March 2025) and Sch. II: R145.07/li aa, R5.95/li, R292.91/li aa, R11.40/10 (R4/fetch/za8/act-45-of-2024.txt, act-3-of-2026.txt). The Namibian notices gazetting the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 SACU rates are not held: the amounts and the SA effective dates are taken as the common rates (grade B).

cit.name: Normal tax on companies
cit.statute: ITA Schedule 4 para. 3 (1) (a) (ii) (30 cents per N$ for years of assessment from 1 Jan 2025; Act 4 of 2024 s. 6 (b))
cit.doc: Schedule 4 para. 3 (1): "the rates of normal tax to be levied in respect of the taxable income derived by a company shall be as follows: (a) on each N$ of taxable income derived from a source other than mining= (i) 31 cents in respect of the year of assessment on or after 1 January 2024; and (ii) 30 cents in respect of any year of assessment on or after 1 January 2025". Mining (37,5 cents) and diamond rates not modelled.
notes: ITA Schedule 4 para. 3 (1) (a) (ii): 30 % for years of assessment from 1 Jan 2025 (non-mining)

by company.sector: 'mining' 37,5 % (para 3 (1) (b)), 'diamondMining' 55 % (para 3 (1) (c), 50 % plus the 10 % surcharge), on all the company's taxable income (the model does not split mining from other income); another sector or none given: 30 % (declared); a 'petroleum' company is taxed under the Petroleum (Taxation) Act, 1991 (Act 3 of 1991), not under this tax: no charge here, listed as grade C (nineteenth pass, kernel 2.7.0 SectorCorp.outside)
unsupported: Petroleum (Taxation) Act, 1991 (Act 3 of 1991): petroleum companies get no charge here and are listed (grade C)
split of mining and other income

sectors.statute: ITA Schedule 4 para. 3 (1) (b) (mining of minerals other than diamonds, and services to licensed miners: 37,5 cents per N$)
ITA Schedule 4 para. 3 (1) (c) (diamond mining: 50 cents per N$ plus a surcharge of 10 % of that tax, 55 %)

outside.statute: the Petroleum (Taxation) Act, 1991 (Act 3 of 1991; in force 30 September 1992, per the ITA's amendment notes)

wht.name: Withholding on payments to non-residents
wht.statute: ITA s. 35A (3) (a) (10 % on management and consultancy fees); s. 45 (non-resident shareholders' tax 10 % / 20 %); twelfth pass: ITA s. 35B (2)-(4) (withholding tax on foreign interest 10 %, final; consolidation as in force 2024-09-16); ITA s. 35 (1)-(2) (withholding tax on royalties 10 %, final; substituted by Act 13 of 2015)
wht.doc: s. 35A (3): "The rate of tax is - (a) 10 per cent of any management fee or consultancy fee specified in subsection (1)"; s. 45: "The rate of tax is - (a) 10 per cent of the amounts specified in section 42 if the beneficial owner is a company which holds directly or indirectly at least 25 per cent of the capital of the company paying the dividends; or (b) 20 per cent of the amounts specified in section 42 in all other cases." Twelfth pass (kernel 2.3.0 grade-C withholding): interest 10 %: ITA s. 35B (2)-(4) (withholding tax on foreign interest 10 %, final; consolidation as in force 2024-09-16); royalty 10 %: ITA s. 35 (1)-(2) (withholding tax on royalties 10 %, final; substituted by Act 13 of 2015)

rules.statute: ITA s. 45 (a) (10 %, company holding at least 25 %)
ITA s. 35B (2)-(4) (withholding tax on foreign interest 10 %, final; consolidation as in force 2024-09-16)
ITA s. 35 (1)-(2) (withholding tax on royalties 10 %, final; substituted by Act 13 of 2015)
